description: A single-panel table rendered as an image, listing the chemical composition and two derived thermodynamic parameters for three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steels. The header row reads "CSiMnCrSNiPFeMoVW mass percentage" spanning the first twelve columns, followed by two further columns headed δ_r and ΔH_mix (kJ/mol). The element columns are individually labelled C, Si, Mn, Cr, S, Ni, P, Fe, Mo, V and W, all in mass percent. The three rows are Sample 1, Sample 2 and Sample 3. Sample 1: C 0.45, Si 0.19, Mn 1.53, Cr 14, S 0.01, Ni 0, P 0.014, Fe 83.806, Mo 0, V 0, W 0, δ_r 0.0542, ΔH_mix −0.914. Sample 2: C 0.53, Si 0.4, Mn 1.9, Cr 5.3, S 0.01, Ni 1.13, P 0.013, Fe 89.277, Mo 0, V 0.25, W 1.19, δ_r 0.0595, ΔH_mix −1.213. Sample 3: C 0.15, Si 0.5, Mn 1.5, Cr 5.2, S 0, Ni 1.2, P 0, Fe 89.7, Mo 1.5, V 0.25, W 0, δ_r 0.0335, ΔH_mix −0.451. Compositions are near-balance Fe (83.8–89.7 mass%) with 5.2–14 mass% Cr; δ_r ranges 0.0335–0.0595 and ΔH_mix is negative for all three alloys (−0.451 to −1.213 kJ/mol). The table defines the alloy set used for model validation.

subfigures.description: A single table with an 11-element mass-percentage header (C Si Mn Cr S Ni P Fe Mo V W), plus δ_r and ΔH_mix (kJ/mol) columns, giving the composition of Sample 1, Sample 2 and Sample 3 Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys.

observations.observation: The table reports three alloys labelled Sample 1, Sample 2 and Sample 3 with compositions in mass percentage.
The element columns are headed C, Si, Mn, Cr, S, Ni, P, Fe, Mo, V and W.
Sample 1 has Cr 14 mass%, C 0.45, Si 0.19, Mn 1.53 and Fe 83.806 mass%, with Ni, Mo, V and W all zero.
Sample 2 has Cr 5.3 mass%, C 0.53, Si 0.4, Mn 1.9, Ni 1.13, V 0.25, W 1.19 and Fe 89.277 mass%.
Sample 3 has Cr 5.2 mass%, C 0.15, Si 0.5, Mn 1.5, Ni 1.2, Mo 1.5, V 0.25 and Fe 89.7 mass%, with S, P and W given as 0.
Sample 1 contains the highest Cr level (14 mass%) and the lowest Ni (0) of the three alloys.
The δ_r column lists 0.0542 for Sample 1, 0.0595 for Sample 2 and 0.0335 for Sample 3.
The ΔH_mix column lists −0.914 kJ/mol (Sample 1), −1.213 kJ/mol (Sample 2) and −0.451 kJ/mol (Sample 3); all three values are negative.
Sample 2 has the most negative ΔH_mix (−1.213 kJ/mol) and the largest δ_r (0.0595) of the three alloys.
The header text 'CSiMnCrSNiPFeMoVW mass percentage' spans the element columns, indicating all listed values are mass percentages.
The caption states the table gives the mass percentages of the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys used for model validation.
